newsitem.title: TURKEY: Tofas in more production stoppages.
newsitem.headline: Tofas in more production stoppages.

text.p: Turkey's leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi, equally owned by Italy's Fiat Auto and Turkish Koc conglomerate, said it would halt production in the first three days of this week.

Due to continuing slowdown in car sales and rising inventories, Tofas will also stop production in the last week of October which includes a 1-1/2-day official holiday, the company said in a statement sent to the Istanbul Stock Exchange.
Employees will receive 76 percent of their wages during the stoppages which total seven work days.
Tofas had resumed production on October 7 after a two-week halt from September 24 due to sharply lower demand.

Car makers, parts producers and labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector have been angered by government plans to ease car imports as part of its two revenue-raising packages unveiled in the last three months.

A cabinet decree to allow Turkish workers abroad who deposit at least 50,000 marks for one-year at the central bank to bring in cars with a maximum age of four years without paying customs duties was not approved by President Suleyman Demirel.

But Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has said the government was determined to go ahead with the project although producers have said expectations of cheaper car imports caused already slack domestic car demand to further contract.
Turkey's car output slumped by 26 percent from a year ago to 18,540 in September. Car production was 155,614 in the first nine months, down three percent from the same 1995 period.
